utterances.text: This house, this Smajl Haradinaj's house, up until the time of the shoot-out at the Haradinaj compound on the 24th of March, up until that period of time, had the house been vacant? Do I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes, the house had stood empty up until that time, until we were taken away.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right. Anyway. On this day you were taken there, and you said you were taken up to the first floor. Tell the Trial Chamber what -- how events transpired after that.

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: When we went up to the top floor, just to the right there is a narrow corridor and a small room, and that's where Dragoslav was taken. Vesko and I were left to wait outside in the corridor.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And what could you see and hear following Dragoslav being taken into the room?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: When I came in, I saw certain young men clean their weapons and oil their rifles, regular maintenance if you like. They'd probably been given those weapons in those very days. I saw a number of young soldiers go up and go into the guest-room.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Now, this room that you call the guest-room, is that the room that Dragoslav was taken into?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: No, no. Not now. He was first taken to this small room 3 by 2, I think. It certainly was no larger than that, 3 by 2 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Okay. So just so it's all clear for everyone in the courtroom, you're up on the first floor, you're in a corridor, there's a guest-room and also a small -- small room?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: Small room, and there's a small, narrow corridor separating the two rooms.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Okay. Right. Now, Veselin you said was taken into the small room. Did you hear him from where you were placed? Could you hear him?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: Not Veselin; Dragoslav was. At first, Dragoslav was the one who was taken into that small room.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes, I apologise, that was my mistake. Dragoslav was taken into the small room. Could you hear him from where you were placed?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: We could hear him.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you told the Trial Chamber how events unfolded, and I want you to also tell the Trial Chamber not only what you could see but what you could hear as well.

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: A short while later Dragoslav got sick inside the room, and he was thrown out; after that they took Veselin inside. I could hear Veselin's screams and moans.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: This expression "Dragoslav got sick," any idea how he got sick?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: It wasn't until later that I found out that Dragoslav had been offered some coffee, which he drank. It was probably because of the previous beating that he had sustained that complications arose and --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Witness, Witness, just slow down and I want to get more detail than I think you are providing. You've told us that you took him -- that all three of you went up to this first floor. And you've told us there's this guest-room there and you've told us that there's a small room. Now, you've also told us that Dragoslav was taken into the small room.

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: In the small room, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Now, when Dragoslav was inside that small room, what could you hear with your ears? What could you hear?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: Well, screams that followed after the blows. I don't know what -- I don't know what actually happened inside, but I could hear the screams.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And who was doing the screaming?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: Dragoslav, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Thank you. That's what I wanted to know. Now, how long did that go on for?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: Well, I couldn't really tell you how long it took.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: When you next saw Dragoslav, what was his condition and his appearance?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: Dragoslav could not breathe. This is when they decided to throw him out into the corridor. He was pale, clutching his stomach, and at one point, he simply had to lie down on the concrete floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did he have any blood on him?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: There was some blood on his face but not a lot.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: After he was thrown into the corridor, what happened to you and your cousin Veselin?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: Then Veselin was taken into the room. They started beating him. After a while, they brought me in, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Okay. Now, just pause it there. Firstly, how do you know that they started beating him, too, if you weren't there? Could you hear anything?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I could hear his screams while he was -- while I was in the small corridor.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And, eventually, you said that you were -- that after a while, they brought you in. Now, when you first went into the room, what did you see?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: I saw Veselin, he was facing a corner. He was naked to his waist. After that, when I got in, Zeqir Nimonaj, who was there, ordered me to take off my clothes down to the waist.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you do that?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And what happened then?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: Well, then they started questioning me. There was a small desk. As far as I can remember, Besnik was sitting there, Besnik Haradinaj. He is Rasim Haradinaj's son, and that was Ramush Haradinaj's cousin. And he asked questions that we had to answer, and if they were not happy with the answer, then they would continue beating us.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Were you struck? Were you struck and beaten by these men?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes, yes. They beat us. We couldn't and we didn't dare beat them. There were two other people there who beat us all the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I'd just like to get a few more details about this scene. Firstly, how was Besnik -- how was Besnik and the two men whom you didn't know, how were they dressed?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: Besnik was in a black uniform, a military-type uniform; and the other two, as far as I can remember, they were wearing camouflage uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And what about Zeqir Nimonaj, what was he -- how was he dressed?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: Zeqir Nimonaj was in a camouflage uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you see any KLA insignia on any of the men in that room?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes, all of them wore KLA insignia.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And were you beaten with -- how were you beaten, just with fists and boots or were instruments used or a combination? Tell us precisely?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: Zeqir had some kind of a rod with a wooden handle, and from this handle there protruded some kind of a rubber rod of some kind, and it had a spring wound around it. And then at the top there was a lead ball, and it caused a lot of pain, and the blow was really hard even if the person wielding it did not strike very hard. They also struck us with rifle-butts and pistols, and although we were facing the wall for most of the time, we didn't dare look at them. A couple of times I asked Zeqir, Why are you doing this, Zeqir? And he said, Don't mention my name at all. He told me that I was a Chetnik and he cursed my Serbian mother. He was generally verbally abusive towards me.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: During this process, did any other individuals come in, apart from Zeqir, Besnik, and the two other unknown KLA men? Did anyone else come in or make an appearance?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: Well, people would come in and out, but I personally could not see who it was that got in or got out. But several people got in, then some other people would get out. I could hear their foot steps as they walked in and out the door.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Eventually the beating must have ended. Can you give us an idea of, if you can of course, of how long you were in there being beaten in this fashion?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: Well, I can't remember now, but it lasted for a long time. After a while, Veselin and I were thrown out and we saw Dragoslav lying there. He was half dead.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Thank you. And now I'd like you to give the Trial Chamber appearances, please. Were you -- do you know if you had blood on your face or blood on your clothing or -- and indeed blood on your torso or legs?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, there was no blood on me. Dragoslav was already lying in a pool of blood. He had vomited blood, and he had a head injury. I hadn't seen until that moment that he had this injury on his nose. It was only then that I realised he had been injured on the nose, and he was unconscious. I tried to help him, and the soldiers that were guarding us in this same corridor, there would be at any given time five, six, or ten soldiers guarding us, sometimes only two of them, but they would not allow me to assist him. Every time I wanted to help Dragoslav, I had to ask for their permission and then they would either give it to me or not. Until the time that we left, they would approach us. They would slap us, hit us; to be more specific, there was this guy who was called the Russian. That was the first time that I saw him there in Glodjane, he slapped us and he took some kind of a rod or a baton and he hit Dragoslav even though he was unconscious, then he hit Veselin, and then he hit me. Because it seemed to him that I was the fittest person there of all of them, and he beat me until he got tired. He beat me until he broke out in a sweat with this metal baton. I didn't dare to look up at all. I kept my head down all the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Thank you. By the time this had all gone on, what was the visible condition of Veselin?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: Well, how to explain to you? Veselin was in a lot of pain. He had blood on his ears. I don't know how to actually describe him, the condition he was in.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Right. But could you see blood on his face -- around his ears?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes, around his ears there was blood. I don't know why, I can't remember now.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Did Dragoslav regain consciousness?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: Dragoslav would drift in and out of consciousness all the time. The moment Dragoslav went in a coma, I would try and help him and then some soldiers would not allow me to do so. They would hit me with the rifle-butts. It was terrible. I had to watch him. I thought he was dying. I couldn't help him. So he was -- he would lose consciousness, then he would come to.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, your ordeal must have ended. I'd like you now to turn your attention as to how eventually you got out of that place. You've described in detail the beatings. Did you eventually leave the place?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes. At one moment, Nasim Haradinaj approached us, and he said that we would be released and that they had decided to give us a vehicle. I assumed then that this was my Lada because Dragoslav's Mazda 626 was a relatively newer vehicle. And I said, Nasim, If you want to kill us, kill us here. Don't torture us any longer if you want to release us. And then he said -- he asked me, Where do you think I should take you first? And then I told him that if they were really in earnest about letting us go, that they should take us to the village of Babaloc because some Serbian refugees who had come from Albania were living there at the time. And at that moment, he and I and a third person went towards the house to take the car, one of my cars -- one of the two cars. And as we headed there, we were talking as if nothing had happened in the meantime. He asked me, Why did you leave the house? Why didn't we join them? Why didn't we stay there? He said, Well, we should -- you should stay here, you should go to our schools, and so on. And en route to Ramush Haradinaj's house that I described earlier on the small path, I saw my Lada car and it was riddled with bullet-holes. The wheels were on the rims, all the tires had been taken away. And then Nasim said, Well, all you have to do is fix it. I tried fixing it, and as soon as I opened --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Okay. Can I just ask you to pause there now? I just want to refer back to part of the narrative, and I just want to clarify a few features of it. Firstly, was the Lada where you had parked it originally?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: No. The Lada was parked in the yard when we got arrested, and now I found it on the path. It was not a road, it was a path that led to Ramush Haradinaj's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: On the way from this Smajl Haradinaj's house where you had been beaten and tortured, on the way to your car, the Lada, did you recognise anyone? Did you see anyone that you recognised?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes. As we went there, I did see Eljmi Haradinaj [as interpreted] in the yard. He had come earlier and I had seen him -- I saw him there standing with Ramush Haradinaj. There was some other soldiers there standing there in groups of two or three in this large courtyard of Smajl's house. I can't remember whether they were standing there separately or in those groups, but Ramush's father was standing there. That's what I'm sure about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: Is that Hilmi? It says in the transcript "Eljmi" Haradinaj. Is it Hilmi, the father?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Hilmi, yeah, with an H.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And you said that you were sure about him. What about Ramush Haradinaj? You said you saw him standing there with Ramush Haradinaj, are you sure it was Ramush?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes, I'm 100 per cent sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And is that as you were coming out of Smajl Haradinaj's house on the way to the car, on the way to the Lada?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right. Did you manage to get the Lada working?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: No, I tried to fix the Lada, but when I found the jack I realised that I once -- even if I could get it up, that there was some problems, problems -- major problems with the engine, that parts of the engine had been destroyed, and I tried to fix it. And Nasim was standing there maybe 10 or 12 metres away from me and he was looking on. At one moment, he approached me, and he asked me if I could fix it, and I said no, I couldn't. Then we decided to go back to the HQ.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: They decided that I should go back to the headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right. And is that what you did?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And was that -- when you say the "HQ," I take it you're referring to Smajl Haradinaj's house, that place?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes -- well, I wouldn't actually call it the headquarters. I would prefer to call it a prison.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Okay, but that building, Smajl Haradinaj's house?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And did you go back there; and if so, what did you do when you arrived?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: When I got back, I asked Nasim for permission to get Dragoslav down. When I got upstairs, Dragoslav was not in the corridor where he had been when I left -- when I'd left. I found him in the guest-room next to the door, and I said to Veselin that we should get him downstairs. Nobody paid any attention to us. Nobody beat us anymore. I was able to get Dragoslav down the stairs. We stood there in the courtyard for a while, and then Hilmi, Ramush's father, approached us. He offered us some food and something to drink, and we said that we couldn't because of the beating that we had undergone, we didn't dare. And it didn't occur to us -- we really didn't feel like eating or drinking anything. We stood there I don't know how long, and then we started walking, although ostensibly we were supposed to wait there for an official car to come and take us there. So we started walking towards the house where, as Nasim had explained to me, they would have to carry out a search of our property. And as we left Glodjane, a tractor came out, that must have been a fourth or a fifth house in the village, a tractor came out of one of the houses. I know -- I don't know the name of this man, but I know which house he was from, and we asked him to take Dragoslav with -- on the tractor because he was in such a bad shape. First, they put him outside, but because he was in such a bad shape, they moved him into the -- into cabin of the tractor. And I walked with Nasim behind. When we got to the house, Nasim ordered me -- well, there was a fig tree in our yard, and my mother would put corn-stalks around it every winter to prevent it from freezing.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can I ask you to pause there? Did they search the fig tree and the house for weapons?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Right. Any weapons found?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes, I was about to explain all this. They thought that there was something hidden at the fig tree because of this amount of corn-stalks around it. He handed me a knife, and I started cutting the rope or the string that it was tied up with, and then when they saw that there was nothing there but corn-stalks --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Okay. Thanks for that, and you've taken us -- you've made up some ground in time. Thanks for giving us that. Just a couple of questions. You've told us that they were -- said they had to search the house, and you've told us about them searching the tree and so on. All I want to know is: At the end of all of this process, did they find any weapons in your house?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Now, think back to the time that you were in -- well, right up until that point, had any of them, Nasim or any of the men who first came into your house or any of the interrogators at the Smajl Haradinaj's house, had they asked you any questions about the activities of your mother, what she was up to in the preceding months?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: No, they did not ask any questions about my mother.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Fine. Okay. Did they make any accusations against you -- well, let me withdraw that. Did they make any accusations against your mother?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: No, not against our mother, but they kept on calling us spies all the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did they ever provide details of the spy -- your spying activities?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: No. They had their suspicions because -- as our brother was a police officer, they suspected us of relaying information to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did they say that or is that what you think? That's what I want to know.

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: Well, that's what I thought --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: -- that these were the suspicions that they had because I can't understand why anybody would call us spies for no reason.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: So I want to be clear about that. That's something you thought; correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Sorry, just before my learned friend pursues that line of questioning, can he be clear about what it is that he is saying is something the witness thought, because the transcript makes it clear that the witness was indicating that he, or they, had been called spies on that occasion. In other words, had been orally accused of spying. MR. DI FAZIO: Well, I'll -- let me approach it this way.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: In your answer you said: "No, they" -- I asked you: "Did they ever provide details of the -- your spying ...?" And you said: "No. They had their suspicions because -- as our brother was a police officer, they suspected us of relaying information to him."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, I had some difficulties in understanding your last observation because what I understood, there are two issues: First of all, what they said, that is that they were spying; and the second is why this witness thought they may have said that. And I do understand that the first -- that's at least what his testimony tells me, but let's just verify. Mr. Stojanovic, is it true that they said that you are spies?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, they often said that as they beat us. Zeqir would just say, You spy, you spy, you Chetnik, you Chetnik, and this kind of insults. And that is why -- I mean, that is the only reason that may have prompted them to suspect us of spying. They had no other basis for those accusations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: These are your thoughts and not what they said? They didn't say, You're spies because you relay all the information to your brother, but that's your own thoughts?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, they didn't say that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, that's clear. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right. Let's move on to another topic, your continuation of your narrative of events. You've told us that you made -- you got -- the three of you got back to your place, and the place was searched and the fig tree was searched. Did you eventually leave your house and -- in company with KLA soldiers?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: Before we headed out, this other person who was with Nasim went through the house, although they knew that they had already searched it, turned it over. While we were standing there in the courtyard, Nasim went in and cut a curtain into pieces and used it to blindfold us and to tie our hands. And at one point, an Ascona, an Opel Ascona car, came by, and they put us into this car and took us to Babaloc. And from time to time they would stop, and then they would talk with some people, and they would say, Well, these are good guys. We decided to save their lives. We don't want the bread to kill us, that's what they said. This is a verbatim translation from Albanian. I understand Albanian, so that's what they said. And they kept saying that until all the way down to Babaloc, until they took us out of the car. There they turned the car around. Dragoslav was sitting on the opposite side. They told me I should not turn around, I should not look back, and I should then go to my brother and took his -- take his hand and take him down. For the first hundred metres, we were ordered not to look back, and we were ordered to walk and then we were allowed to run after that distance. Everybody knew there in the camp, in Babaloc, that we would come. The Serbs in Babaloc had been notified by my brother. They saw us arrive, so they come and picked us up in a car and took us to the health centre in Decani. And from there, they transferred us immediately to Pec --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Just hold it there. This -- you said the Serbs in Babaloc had been notified by your brother, and they saw you arrive and came and picked you up in a car. Which brother notified them, and how did he know to do that? What had he notified them of?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: The brother in the Lada had notified them that we had left -- or the brother named Vlado told them that morning, because the police no longer went to that area. So the assumption was that we had been captured because the original deal had been for us to be back within an hour or an hour and a half at most.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Right. Thank you. I understand. So you're not aware of your brother actually passing on any message; you were late, you had expected to be back sooner. Do I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: Precisely, precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And this area that you moved into, this area around Babaloc - it might be an obvious question but I want to know the answer - was that an area that was where Serb police still maintained control and Serbs were able to live?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes, there's a settlement there of refugees, Serbs, who had fled from Albania. The UN and the state had built a number of houses for them in the area which they moved into and --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Fine, fine. Thank you. Now, when you first got out of the Lada, when you first got out of the Lada, were you all blindfolded or not?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes, we were all blindfolded. Nasim undid these one by one and simply took them off.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And what did Nasim say to you at that point after he'd taken off your blindfolds?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: As I said a while ago he said, Don't look back. If you look back you'll be fired at by our check-points. Our people are monitoring your movements, that sort of thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Okay. I take it you took his advice and kept walking?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: Very much so. We did exactly what we'd been told. I was afraid that if I were to do anything differently, what he had predicted would come true.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right. And I don't think this is in dispute, your brother was -- he went to hospital and was treated in hospital. Did you also receive medical attention?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: I received medical attention in Pec. I was offered to remain in hospital, but it was for the security reasons that I refused. I did have to go back for treatment with Veselin every day.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you very much for answering my questions? MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Di Fazio. Before I give an opportunity for cross-examination, is there agreement among the parties where Smajl's house is? Because I've heard a lot of details, names of schools, et cetera, but it's still unclear whether on any of the evidential material, either on the photographs, we can find it because -- or is it part of the compound we found on the aerial photograph? It's not clear to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I can indicate to Your Honours this much without obviously giving evidence at this stage myself --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, if the parties agree --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It hasn't been the subject of any formal agreement I'm sure it will be possible for us to discuss between ourselves but it's in the village of Glodjane as opposed to outside near the border with Dubrava.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we perhaps show the witness the picture of the village, the aerial picture, and ask him whether he can --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Because the same question was put to the other witness, but he was not able to -- MR. DI FAZIO: I've got no problem with that at all. I encourage it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: At least so we know where it is. Yes. But now I have to find which exactly -- it's the arrow -- MR. DI FAZIO: 35 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think it's 35 -- 2 or -- MR. DI FAZIO: 35, I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, 35. Could P35 be shown to the witness. Oh, no, it's not P35. I take it it's P32. P35 seems the ... or isn't even -- MR. DI FAZIO: I wasn't quite sure which one actually, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The one where you can see houses, et cetera. MR. DI FAZIO: The larger overall view?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, I didn't have this one in mind as a matter of fact but there is a --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Could perhaps we proceed with cross-examination and then clarify --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- that issue after the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, now I also remember what the problem was. During the opening statement you used a far clearer picture of the village which gives a better possibility for orientation. If that could be in one way -- I see that was U014-3045 in the photographs that has been shown to us during the -- or at least was in the bundle provided to us in the -- but please proceed, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, I want to start, if I may, by asking you some questions about the evidence that you've given us of your knowledge of the Haradinaj brothers going back to the times when you lived in Dubrava before you left for your military service in 1982. Now, first of all, you gave evidence a little earlier on today that you had known Ramush Haradinaj ever since you started in fifth grade at school when you had been transferred from school in Gjakove to Irzniq before moving on again to school in Decane. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: School to Rznic, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You told us that you were transferred to Irzniq in the fifth grade. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And how old would you have been then, in the fifth grade?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: Fifth grade, about 12 -- I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And how long were you at this school at Irzniq before you transferred to Decane for the remainder of your schooling? How long were you at the village school in Irzniq?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: Three, three years.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So between roughly the ages of 12 and 15?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And I think it's common ground that Ramush Haradinaj's just about four and a half years younger than you are, so presumably during that time he would have been something between 7 and 11 while you were at school together, at the same school?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And then you moved off to school in Decane. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And that's where you stayed until you left Dubrava for your military service in 1982. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: I did go to school in Decani, but I went home every day. I commuted between Dubrava and Decani. It was only during school that I would be in Decani, and after that I would go back home.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, I understand, it was a day school. And then in 1982, you left Dubrava for your military service; yes?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And how long was your military service for?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: 12 months.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And immediately after your military service, did you then go to study at the university in Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: As far as I remember, I spent about two months in Kosovo, after which I went to Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And I think you didn't finish your university in Belgrade, but you did then at some point start work --

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: No, I didn't. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But you did then, I think, start working in Belgrade in a shoe factory for some time. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And perhaps it doesn't matter exactly when that was, but could we put it -- summarise it this way: You didn't return to live in Dubrava until 1995. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So going back to the time when you left, if I've got my calculations correct you were not living in Dubrava for a period of about 13 years from 1982 through to 1995, you were not -- that was not your permanent home during that 13-year period. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And at the time you left for your military service, Ramush Haradinaj would have been around 13. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: I don't know, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, you --

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: I suppose your calculation must be right.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, to just get a sense of how well you really knew the brothers of the Haradinaj family from the interaction that you'd had with them, how many brothers are there?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: Six. As far as I know, there were six of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And apart from Ramush and Daut, do you know the names of any of the others?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: I said I didn't, didn't I? They were a lot younger; that was why I didn't know them. I knew them as kids from the area. I used to see them every now and then, but I didn't actually know them. They were neighbours after all.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, I'm going to suggest to you that what you've just said is wrong and that they were not kids at all, but that two of them, Luan and Shkelzen, were in their mid and late 20s in 1998; they were just two and four years younger, respectively, than Ramush and older than Daut, they were between the two. Did you know them?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: I was talking about the younger ones. I didn't say anything about the older ones.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not understand the witness's answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you please repeat your answer, Mr. Stojanovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was talking about the younger ones. I said I didn't know those, the younger ones, those.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Do you know or did you know the names of the older ones? Because you were asked the question by Mr. Di Fazio earlier on whether you knew the names of any of the brothers? Did you know the names of the older ones?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: No, no, no, I didn't. By pure coincidence, I went to school with those. Since the move to the new house, I met the two of them and those two I did go to school with.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And so, again, just so that we're clear, is it your evidence that you were not at school with Shkelzen and Luan Haradinaj?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes, I may have been, it just -- I don't remember. For a while they lived in the centre of the village, across the way from Smajl's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Presumably, Mr. Stojanovic, you weren't close friends with this boy who was --

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And just so that I can make the question clear: You weren't close friends with Ramush Haradinaj?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: No, apart from the fact that we travelled together. We didn't talk in any special way or socialise. We weren't on visiting terms. For example, I never went -- I only ever went when his father, Hilmi, came, to mow the lawn. There was this one year, I can't remember specifically when, we had someone who did that for us, so I went over to -- to his house to mow his lawn.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And the other older brothers, did you get to know them at all?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: I probably did, but I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I mean, whilst you were at school - perhaps you can help us with this - did you know the name of Ramush Haradinaj?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I do remember knowing his name.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And do you remember knowing the names of the others while you were at school?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: No. By pure coincidence, Ramush and I come from the same area. There were a few students travelling to school at the same time that we did, and that's why I knew Ramush's name, and that's why I knew Ramush.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I understand that's your evidence, Mr. Stojanovic, and the question I had asked you, and I thought you had answered, was that -- whether the other brothers also went to the school with you, and I thought your evidence was, They may have done, I don't know?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: I don't remember, I simply don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Looking at the 13-year period that you were living away from Dubrava, I just want to be clear, you told us you went back from time to time. Did you ever meet with Ramush Haradinaj when you returned home for your weekend or week-long visits? Did you meet him?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: I don't remember. I wouldn't just go back for the weekend and for a week. Sometimes I would spend my entire annual leave in the area, as long as a month sometimes. So the answer is maybe I did, maybe I didn't, but I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And, again, same question for the other brothers: Do you remember meeting any of the others when you were at home during these periods?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I want to ask you some questions about the 18th of April for a moment. First of all, you told us, I think, that the first shot you heard when you were at the house came from the direction of Dubrava. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: That's correct. That's what I heard. I thought the shot came from Dubrava.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So that would be the opposite side of your house from the house where the Haradinaj compound is?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And then you said you heard a shot coming from the Gllogjan side of the house. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And could you -- could you really tell where specifically that shot -- second shot had come from?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: I don't think I could. The bullet came from the direction of Ramush's house because that part faces the -- or rather, the Glodjane road because we are very close to the road, both Ramush and I. I am just next to the road, and Ramush is a little to the right.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So just to be clear, is it your evidence that that second shot came from the general direction of Gllogjan, but you can't be more specific than that? Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: No, I can't be specific. From Glodjane, yes, that much is true, but I can't say exactly from which.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You told us in your evidence about the period during which you were being walked from your house towards Gllogjan village. And you described a moment when you say that you saw Ramush Haradinaj along the way. Do you remember giving that evidence this morning?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I just want to ask you one or two questions about that, if I can. First of all, you've given various descriptions of that sighting in different statements that you've made at different times, I think, and you've been asked about them quite recently by the Prosecution in a meeting that you had with them about your statement. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: [No audible response].

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And I think in the most recent meeting on the 23rd of March, you were anxious to correct an error in your witness statement, because in your witness statement originally you thought you'd said that you'd seen Ramush Haradinaj standing outside your yard, but you wanted to correct that to say that he was standing outside his yard, the yard of the Haradinaj family compound. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can you just give us a sense, when you say he was standing outside his yard, can you just give us a sense, please, of how close to the house he was, an estimate of the distance between Ramush Haradinaj and his own house?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: I'd be hard-put to be specific about the distance, but when I amended that particular reference about the 23rd of March I'm telling you about that road, I'm not sure how to explain this, the road leading to the house, it's actually closer to his yard than the road itself. The distance is just over a half. I'm not sure what the distance is.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Sorry, don't worry about the length of the road for a moment. We can come to that in a moment, and I've understood what you're saying. There's a roadway that leads from the main road down to the Haradinaj family compound. That's what you're describing, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I just want you to help us, please. The man that you say that you saw, was he standing close to the Haradinaj family compound?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: Who exactly do you have in mind, Ramush or -- I said there was another man, possibly two persons, standing next to him. So do you mean those two, or do you mean Ramush?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, all three of the people you've described if they were standing together. Were they standing close to the Haradinaj house?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: I told you a while ago, they were standing at just over half the way there.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: That's what I wanted to be clear about. So just over halfway along that road that runs from the main road to the Har --

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: That path --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: That path.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: That path.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So just over halfway, do you mean closer to the Haradinaj house or closer to the road?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: Closer to the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So nearly halfway, but closer to the road?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: Closer to the road, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So I wonder if you could help us just for a moment?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Could we bring up, please, Exhibit D24.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, I'm also looking at the clock --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- we need a break soon. I don't know how much time it would take you to start with your next subject but --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm -- I think certainly provided the photograph can be brought up reasonable quickly I can deal with this in a minute or two, I think, if that suits --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And can we please focus in on the roadway.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And you see that just about halfway there's a bend in the road, Mr. Stojanovic. Now, I think you've said that he was just over halfway along and slightly closer to the road. Could you mark for us, please, on the paragraph that position?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We need to give it a new number there. Madam Registrar, the photo to be marked will be ...?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be Exhibit Number D27, marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can I just be clear, can you orientate yourself? Do you know what we're looking at, Mr. Stojanovic, just before you mark it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic has marked it already --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you look at it --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: All right, that's fine -- MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please I think Mr. Emmerson's question needs to be answered because --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, let's -- Mr. Stojanovic, you made a mark, was that by mistake or was that the place where you wanted to mark where these three people were standing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wanted to mark the spot where the three persons were standing.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And do you have any difficulties in orienting yourself on this aerial photograph, or is it perfectly clear to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's difficult, it's difficult. I find it difficult to work with this aerial photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Let me just see if I can help you, Mr. Stojanovic. There's one potential confusion on it. If you look at the Haradinaj compound, there's been building on that since you lived there. But the road that you're looking at is the road that leads from the main road down to the compound. And if we just pull down the picture, pull it out a little, can you see at the bottom left-hand side of the photograph next to the road --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but it has to be done because otherwise the witness can't see it. Yes, Madam Usher, I am aware ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If we zoom out, Mr. Emmerson --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- then we lose the marking, but perhaps that might be not -- be better --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'd like to save the marking, if possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Couldn't it be re-made once the witness has clearly oriented himself? So let's perhaps get rid of this one, have the original photograph again, we keep that then for the same number. We first zoom it out, ask the witness to orient himself, and then ask him to make the marking again.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Do you have the full picture on your screen, Mr. Stojanovic?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: If you look at the road that runs vertically along the left-hand side of the photograph from top to bottom, that is the road that runs -- that is the road that runs from Dubrava towards Gllogjan --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: From top to bottom, it would be the other way around.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: With Dubrava at the bottom and Gllogjan at the top, are you with me?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: This photograph leaves me in the dark --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: -- I can't find my way around these aerial photographs.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, I'm going to help you, Mr. Stojanovic, so that you're absolutely clear. All right. Now, the road that runs along the left-hand side of that photograph going vertically from top to bottom is a road that runs from the top, the Gllogjan direction, down towards the bottom, towards Dubrava. All right. The large building on the right-hand side is the Haradinaj family compound. You can accept that from me?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: As it looks today --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: As it looks today. And the building to the bottom left-hand corner of the photograph, which you can just see on the right-hand side of the road, is the location of your property?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now you've orientated yourself. The road that leads to the Haradinaj compound is the road that you were looking at before that runs from the corner down to a bend roughly halfway and then on to the Haradinaj compound. And perhaps we can look at that again a little larger.

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, let me repeat my question. You gave evidence a few moments ago that when you saw Ramush Haradinaj standing with two other men, they were slightly more than halfway along that road, and you just marked the position for us. Can you tell us, please -- or perhaps I can ask you to do it again. Can you mark for us the position slightly beyond halfway where you say they were?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: Up here, I think that's where I marked it before.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Now, perhaps we can save it --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps in order to find it -- yes, but one second. Could you make it a cross rather than a dot, because it's a very small dot. If you could make that a cross --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, like that. Thank you very much. This will now be D27, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. Perhaps -- working with maps anyhow, I suggest, and we could make it a Defence exhibit, to have U0143045 on the screen which is -- that would then, since it has been produced -- we could make it a Chamber exhibit, but, Mr. Emmerson, we would be quite glad, as well, if it would be D28 for you. That gives a better orientation.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take it that if it's in the village and if the other witness was invited to identify the -- Smajl's house on the -- what I think is D23, but then it should be on this photograph as well. Can you orient yourself, Mr. Stojanovic? Do you see what this is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think it is Glodjane, but it's a little fuzzy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Do you think that you could find Smajl's house on this photograph? And things might be different from what they were at that time, but ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Probably so. There are new houses as far as I can tell, so the shape, the outline, the layout is entirely changed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I do understand that there are new houses. But are you able to find the place where Smajl's house was, from what you remember?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't hear the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you can't find it, just tell us, then we'll just move on. I see you're nodding no.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then the parties are invited -- I don't know whether the house could be found on this picture, but to see whether there could be any agreement so that the Chamber also finds out where it actually happened, or at least at what place the witnesses described as far as where it happened. We will adjourn and resume at 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: In answer to Your Honour's question, the house does not appear on the photograph that Your Honour has drawn our attention to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: We are endeavouring to have available a clear enough aerial photograph which can be the subject of agreement with the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We do not necessarily need a photograph, but at least to know where approximately it's located on the map is fine as well or a detailed map. Was it on the other photograph, because it covers more or less the same area?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I think the answer to that is no. It's certainly not -- it's not in the photograph which is in the spiral-bound volume, which is I think the same photograph as the one that Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, there was a different photograph shown to the witness from a different angle that same village of Glodjane but I didn't see that there was more on that photograph than there is on this one --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I think not. I think, if I may say for Your Honour's information and I'll be corrected if I'm wrong, the building is -- it would be beneath --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- the photograph, in other words behind the position that the aerial photograph has been taken here from and, therefore, off the screen, so further down the road that we see there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But what we're aiming to do is produce something which is easy to see and where it can be marked for Your Honours' assistance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Further on, I was informed that the videolink for -- is not possible for next week. We granted yesterday - and I might come back to that later, within the next half-hour - but technically it seems to be a problem to have that videolink next week and it could only be the week after that. It is just for your information, Mr. Di Fazio, so please get in touch with the registry. MR. DI FAZIO: Well, that might also have wider implications for the sequence of witnesses for next week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Maybe. Could be, yes. MR. DI FAZIO: Do you want to be addressed about that today? I know Mr. Emmerson is interested in the issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, as a matter of fact full communication between the parties is of utmost importance and spending time in court is to be avoided. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes, of course, and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And these are the kind of practical matters, I would say, which are -- we can deal with by just sending copies to the extent acceptable to the Chamber of practical communication between the parties. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes. Well, Mr. Re will surely contact Mr. Emmerson today to discuss that matter. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. Then, Mr. Emmerson, I suggest that what I -- what I suggested to be D28 should not be an exhibit at all. We have -- at this moment, we have the number that is U0143045, we have that on the record and that identifies the photograph shown to the witness. The witness has not been able to orient himself on the photograph, so let's get rid of that, and it saves me the problem of whether we should make it a Chamber exhibit or a Defence or a Prosecution exhibit. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, forget for a moment Smajl Haradinaj's house --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just one moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Going back to the moment when you were walking along the road towards Gllogjan on the 18th of April and you have described seeing Ramush Haradinaj, you say he was with two other people. Are you able to describe those two other people?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: No, I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: In the evidence that you gave a little earlier today --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And for Your Honours' note, it's page 44, line 24.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- you said that at the time you saw Ramush Haradinaj on the side road, there were other neighbours in the area, and you said: "But they kept telling us not to look left and right but just to keep our heads down." Now, I just want to be clear, Mr. Stojanovic, were they telling you not to look left and right and just to keep your heads down as you were walking along the road?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes, on that macadam road.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And is that why you weren't able to see the other two men who were standing with Ramush Haradinaj?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, one was with his back to me and I probably didn't even know the other one.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: The one with his back to you, was he nearer to you than Ramush Haradinaj?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: No, not really with his back to me but with his side. He was turned sideways.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Were there other people on that side road at all, apart from the three of them?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: There was a check-point there, a trench that was considered to be a check-point, and on the left-hand side there were some soldiers coming out of Xhavit's house. I don't recall his last name.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can we try to keep this simple and separate? Xhavit's house, you've told us, is on the opposite side of the main road from the Haradinaj compound, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm not asking you at the moment about people who may have been coming out of Xhavit's house. On the road that leads from the main road down to the Haradinaj compound, is that where you saw soldiers at a check-point?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: You mean the two or some other soldiers?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Let me ask you the question again and avoid any possible confusion. You've told us that the man you thought was Ramush Haradinaj was standing with two soldiers, and you've shown us on the photograph where that was. Leave them aside for a moment. Were there other people on the road, apart from those three?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes, there were quite a few soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And were they nearer to the main road than Ramush Haradinaj or between Ramush Haradinaj and the Haradinaj compound?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: Those soldiers were mostly on the main road.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Were any of them on the side road that leads to the Haradinaj compound?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: I don't think so, but I can't remember all that well.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You told us that there was a check-point or a trench. Was that on the side road?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: It was on the corner. There was a ditch there, so that was at the intersection of the main road and the side road, a trench had been dug there.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And were there soldiers or people, let's put it that way, were there people in the intersection there, standing in the intersection that you have described where the trench was?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: Well, I said that there were quite a few soldiers near the trench, maybe 5 or 10 metres away from the trench, five or ten soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just pause there then, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can we have a look, please, again at a fresh D24. If we could just zoom in, please, on the area of the junction between the two roads.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Stojanovic, looking at the junction there, could you take a pen, please, and mark for us with a line, a straight line, where the trench that you're describing was?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just on one side of the road like that or on both sides?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: I remember that it was on this side. I don't remember it being on the other side because Xhavit's house was here. I don't remember Xhavit's last name. I know him quite well -- in fact, he was a schoolmate. So they were coming out of this house, and this is where the trench was.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Forgive me because my question was ambiguous. When I said "just the one side," if you see where the side road joins the main road, you've drawn for us a red line on the opening which is at the bottom of -- where the side road joins the main road. Was there a trench on the opposite side as well? Don't touch the screen with your pen unless you're making an intentional marking.

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: No, no. I -- I'm not clear. What do you mean from the opposite side? I was coming there from Dubrava with my brother Dragoslav.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Let me explain the question. You're walking from the bottom of this picture along the road towards the top, and you've marked for us --

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And you've marked for us a red line to show the trench at the first corner you come to on the right-hand side. If you were to walk further up the road towards Gllogjan, the other side of that opening is another corner on the road leading down to the Haradinaj compound. Was there a trench there as well or not?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: No, and not as far as I can recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, you've told us that you -- that there were a significant number of men some, I think, 5 or 10 metres from the trench. Can you just show us where the men --

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: To the left, on the left-hand side. This is what I meant when I said that there had been a large number of them there because they had all come out of the house, and I was able to recognise Zeqir Nimonaj there.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So could you just mark for us just with a number 1 where those men were standing.

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Were there any other people on the side road, apart from Ramush Haradinaj and the two people he was speaking to?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: As I already said, I don't remember but I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can you show us, please, where you were when you looked over and saw him? Can you mark for us, please, with an X on this map and perhaps it might be a good idea to do it in different colour.

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: Somewhere here in the middle of the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: That's fine. That's fine. It's already done. So the X that you've marked on that map shows where you were standing at the time, does it?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes, but let me note here that this road appears much shorter in real life than it does here on this aerial photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, we can measure the exact distance in due course with the markings that you've given us, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can that please be marked for identification?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, that would be ... ?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be then Exhibit Number D28, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I want to ask you just briefly, before this day when the last time was that you had seen or spoken to Ramush Haradinaj? And before you answer that question, I'm going to suggest to you that Ramush Haradinaj was not in Kosovo between 1991, was not living there between 1991, and the end of February 1998. So he wasn't living in the house there during that period.

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: I don't recall when it was that I saw him last.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can I come then, please --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And we can remove that exhibit now. It's finished with for the time being.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can I come then, please, to a later stage of the events that you've described when you were taken out of Smajl Haradinaj's house to go back to your house and to fix the car that was broken. You've told us in your evidence that when you came out of the house, you saw Hilmi Haradinaj in the yard of Smajl Haradinaj's house. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And was that the first time that you'd seen Hilmi Haradinaj that day?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: When, on the 18th of April, did you first see Hilmi Haradinaj?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: When he brought some juice for Dragoslav.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Was that before you were taken out into the yard to go and fix the car?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: I think so, but I can't remember exactly. It was in the corridor, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You've told us about an occasion when Nasim Haradinaj came and told you that you were going to be released. I want to ask you whether that occasion coincided with when you first saw Hilmi Haradinaj; in other words, did you see Hilmi Haradinaj before or after or roughly at the same time as you were told that you were going to be released?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: I don't remember. I think it was after Nasim Haradinaj, but I don't remember exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: When you saw him - that is Hilmi Haradinaj - outside in the yard, were there other people in the yard apart from him and the man you identified as Ramush Haradinaj? Were there other people in the yard apart from them?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: How many?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: I couldn't give you the figure because they were standing there in groups, small groups, and Smajl's courtyard is quite large. So I couldn't give you the approximate figure.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Again, can you give us a sense of how many people there were?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: No, no, I really couldn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And where was Hilmi when you saw him in the yard?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: Opposite a gate. I don't know how far from the gate he was, though. Not more than 10 or 15 metres, that would be my estimate. I'm talking about the main entrance, the main gate.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And were you taken by Nasim out of the building and directly out of the yard, or were you held in the yard for a period of time?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: We were standing there for a short while in the courtyard.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Again, can you help us at all with any sense of how long that would have been?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: No, no, I can't. I really can't, but we were standing there for a short while.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Do you know what Shkelzen Haradinaj looked like at this point in time?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: No. Shkelzen, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Or one of the older Haradinaj brothers. At this point in time, you didn't know what his appearance would look like?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: No, as I've already said.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I wonder, if I may, to ask you some questions about, first of all, a newspaper interview that you gave. And we have -- we have --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: For this purpose, it would be helpful to have on the screen D25 in the English translation. Now, if I can please hand the witness a hard copy of the original because it's much easier to read in hard copy than on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Haradinaj [sic], that is a copy of a newspaper article published on the 24th of April, 1998, in a Serbian magazine called "Illustrojana Politika," and it contains a lengthy direct interview with you in which you are quoted. And I've marked for you with a highlighter a heading which corresponds in our translation with the words: "We weren't armed ...?"

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So for Your Honours, that's page 3 of the translation. If we could bring that up on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, do you remember giving an interview to a newspaper or magazine shortly after this incident took place?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And do you recognise in the passage that's set out there the words that you used?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm very happy to give you an opportunity, if you want to read the whole article. We've obviously had a chance to look at it in translation. There's just a couple of questions I want to put to you about it, if I may. First of all, there's no mention in this interview of you having seen Ramush Haradinaj on that day. Do you know why that is?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes. Nobody asked me at the time about him.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see, but there is quite a detailed description, Mr. Stojanovic, of what happened in your house. And you can see that, I think, just --

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: There isn't that much detail provided, just the names of the people who beat me. I'm not talking about the names I saw; I'm talking about the names that beat me.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, that's -- that was going to be my next question because if you find the heading that says: "They took off their masks" --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: That's our page 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- you describe what happened in the house. I just wanted to check one matter with you, because you've given evidence to us that Daut Haradinaj, a man you recognised, was amongst those who burst into the house and took part in the beating. But I'm just going to put it to you, there's no mention in this newspaper article of Daut Haradinaj.

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: That may as well be the case. I have no idea what the journalists wrote. I am certain that Daut was among them. Journalists can include or omit whatever they like. It's not my place to judge that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can you find that heading again, please: "They blindfolded us ..."

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: In the English translation, the words immediately beneath that read as follows, and this is you describing what happened at Smajl Haradinaj's house: "At about 4.00 in the afternoon, the neighbour whose house it was, Nasim, arrived and told us that they were going to release us." And then this: "He was probably their boss."

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes. At that moment, and in most other cases, that was how they addressed or greeted all of the Haradinajs, not just Nasim. What's more, even the young Haradinaj who questioned us was addressed the same way.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I was going to come back to him in a moment or two. Does that accurately record what you said, that Nasim was probably their boss?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: That was what I assumed at the time, but I wasn't certain that he was the boss. Whenever he came by, the other soldiers always saluted him. All the soldiers who were wearing the black berets were saluted, so that was what caused me to get that particular impression.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Does that mean you -- if that's an accurate record, you don't suggest that he was one of a number of people who were in charge; if that's an accurate record of what you said, you seem to be suggesting that he was the person, as far as you could see, who was in charge?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: No, no, that's not what I'm saying.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Could we look then, please, at Rule 65 ter --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What I'm saying is he was one of the men in charge, one of those in charge.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Could we look now, please, at Rule 65 ter number 1146. And for Your Honours' assistance, this is another one of those reports that is already part of Exhibit P5 but is individually identified.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps we then do the same as we did before --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: A new --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- and give that -- give that an additional number. Madam Registrar, that would be ...?
