utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be Exhibit Number D29, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Stojanovic, I'm going to have to read this document or passages of it to you, because it's not available in Serbian. This is a report that was filed by a woman called Marijana Andjelkovic, who worked for an organisation called the Humanitarian Law Centre. And as we can see on our document, on the second page --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Perhaps we could call that up and the second paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- this report is based on an interview that Marijana Andjelkovic conducted with you on the 25th of April at a cafe in Decane on the road to the Decani monastery. So this is an interview that took place the day after the article we've just looked at was published.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Does Your Honour have the passage?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Actually, the same day. Wasn't it the 25th?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Your Honour's quite right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: But --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Your Honour's quite right.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So this was an interview that took place on the same day that that magazine article was published. And I just want to ask you one or two questions about this because to be absolutely fair to you, I need to take you through one or two passages slowly. You describe - and I'm now looking at the second paragraph under the heading: "Statement by Mijat Stojanovic" - you're recorded here as describing the arrival of yourselves, that is your brother and yourself, at the house; the start of the shooting; the fact that it went on for 40 minutes; the fact that you weren't armed; the fact that they came into the yard and you decided to give yourselves up; the fact that your brother Dragoslav opened the door; and that 10 or 15 soldiers barged in. And then it goes on as follows: "They hit Dragoslav with a rifle-butt and kicked him. He fell down. They ordered Veselin and me to get down on the floor beside Dragoslav. They beat us, too. When Nasim Haradinaj came in the beating stopped for a moment. He said to them not to beat us, but they went on anyway." And then it goes on to describe you being thrown out in the yard and taken to the headquarters. So in this interview, also as recorded, you made no mention of Daut Haradinaj being present in the house, but you did mention Nasim Haradinaj being present in the house. Can you help us with that at all?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: First and foremost, I've never even heard of this lady. I can say it categorically that I never gave any kind of interview to her. I gave three interviews to the lady from the Humanitarian Rights Fund, but not to this one. I am prepared to confront her any time.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Stojanovic, I don't want to put you in -- at a disadvantage. It may be that you're confusing names, but the lady who took your statement and made notes of it has given evidence in this court. Perhaps you didn't recall her name, but from the Humanitarian Rights Foundation, as you call it, Humanitarian Law Centre I think is its proper name, the lady from that organisation who interviewed you has given evidence before this court with her notebook about the interview with you from which this report is drawn. So I don't want to put you in a difficult position here. You did give an interview, as you've just told us, to a lady from what you call the Humanitarian Rights Foundation, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: What I'm saying is only the extent of my memory. I don't think I ever spoke to this lady.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: I can't entirely rule out the possibility that I did, but not as far as I remember. There was a single interview that occurred in a cafe, and this was for a TV station from Slovakia, possibly from the Czech Republic, that country. It was in a cafe, that's where I gave it, to the extent that I now remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, don't worry about the name of the person. You've told us just a few moments ago you did give interviews to a lady from the Humanitarian Rights Foundation. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: A while ago I said I didn't, didn't I? That's not what I remember saying a while ago. I think I said I didn't speak to her.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You said a few moments ago, Mr. Stojanovic: "I gave three interviews to the lady from the Humanitarian Rights Foundation but not this one."

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: No. I said a total of three interviews about the incident. I didn't say who I gave those to, and now I'm mentioning a different one. The first one was in the "Illustrojana Politika" papers and the other one was to those people from Slovakia, the Czech Republic, and the third interview that I gave was for a TV station, an America one, I'm not sure, at the Decani monastery.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: All right, let me be absolutely clear with you on this, Mr. Stojanovic. Are you saying that you did not give an interview to a lady from a human rights organisation or that you don't know one way or the other?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: Not to the extent that I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: All right. Well, then let me ask you some questions on that understanding between us. The document that we're looking at makes a number of references to Nasim Haradinaj. It describes him as turning up at the time when you were inside your house. It describes him being present when you were first taken to Smajl Haradinaj's house. It describes him coming back in the afternoon and telling you that you were going to be let go. It describes him accompanying you back to your house to check your Lada, and it describes him telling you that they would drive you to Babaloc and he would come along to guarantee your safety. Now, in summary - and I'll take it in summary - each time you refer to Nasim -- I'm sorry, each time Nasim Haradinaj is referred to in this document, he is referred to as telling the other people present not to hit you, not to hurt you? Now, first of all, do you remember Nasim Haradinaj being present in the house when you were first assaulted there?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: He came after a while, after a brief while. Difficult to say, but I think after about 15 or 20 minutes Nasim came by.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And was he telling the other people not to beat you?

utterances.speaker: MIJAT STOJANOVIC.
utterances.text: He was telling the others, but he was also winking an eye at them outside in the yard, letting them know that they could go on with the beating.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Did --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson -- I'm looking at the clock.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I need two or three minutes as well, so therefore usually I ask for a suitable moment, but I would like to invite you to stop. Mr. Stojanovic -- Mr. Emmerson, could you give us an indication how much time you would still need tomorrow?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, I would have thought certainly no longer than half an hour, probably less.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, then other counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: At present I don't expect that I will be examining this witness, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Harvey.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I shall not be examining this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio, any idea? MR. DI FAZIO: Four to five minutes in re-examination, if that -- as things stand at the moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, of course. Mr. Stojanovic, we would like to see you back tomorrow morning, and I instruct you not to speak with anyone about the testimony you have given until now and you are still about to give. We hope that we can conclude your testimony tomorrow morning. Madam Usher, could you escort Mr. Stojanovic out of the courtroom. I would like to deliver a decision of the Chamber on the videolink.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is a decision regarding the Prosecution's partly confidential motion of the 23rd of March, 2007, for testimony to be heard via video-conference link. The Defence has not opposed the motion as such but has urged further to explore the possibility to taking over obligations by that witness -- of that witness by professionals. The Chamber reiterates its approach to video-conferences, as set out in its written decision filed on the 21st of March. The test is as follows: The witness must be unable or have good reasons to be unwilling to come to the Tribunal; B, if the testimony of the witness must be sufficiently important to make it unfair to the requesting party to proceed without it; and C, the accused must not be prejudiced in the exercise of his or her right to confront the witness. In the present case, the Chamber has carefully reviewed the confidential materials submitted by the Prosecution with its motion and is satisfied that the witness in question has good reasons to be unwilling to come to The Hague. The witness has ongoing obligations to another person that cannot easily be relieved to allow the witness to travel to The Hague. The Chamber finds that upon striking a fair balance the advantages of hearing that witness -- that testimony be given in The Hague and the additional burden to have the obligation of this witness to be taken over by professionals results in our finding that the witness can give his evidence through videolink. This, therefore, as the parties know already because it was informally communicated to them, the Chamber hereby grants the motion, and this concludes the ruling of the Chamber on this matter. Yes, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Defence, and I think also the Prosecution, owe Your Honours a pleading today; that is to say, a response in respect to the recording of video -- of proofing sessions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: We are significantly advanced with it. We would hope to be able to file it today, but since we are trying to avoid more than one set of Defence filings and since there is really quite a lot of material in the Prosecution's main filing, it is conceivable that we might spill over until tomorrow. Would Your Honours grant us that grace, if it's necessary?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Di Fazio, a couple of hours? MR. DI FAZIO: That's not a problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then it's granted, if necessary.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I remind the parties that we said the next witness who is at this moment present in The Hague ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: From what I understand, the examination of the present witness should be easily concluded within the first session tomorrow morning. The next witness is scheduled for one hour and a half, so therefore if we would be really efficient, we might be able to conclude the testimony of the next witness, unless, Mr. Emmerson, I'm not fully aware whether you needed more time for the next witness. If not --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Unless there's something that I'm not expecting in his testimony --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, okay --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- I would have thought it was possible we may well conclude him tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That means that if we are efficient, we could try to conclude this witness tomorrow, which would prevent us from sitting on Thursday. So therefore, if the parties would really focus very much on what is most important and not be repetitious in any way in their questioning, then we might be able to -- MR. DI FAZIO: Well, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- conclude tomorrow. MR. DI FAZIO: Mr. Kearney is probably best placed to advise you about that. I think it's going to be brief, but he can tell you more.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I will do my best to get through the material as quickly as possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Di Fazio, you are aware that if you are taking more time, Defence might take more time as well. We might end up having to sit also on Thursday. So it's finally up to you. We adjourn and -- until tomorrow, the 28th of March, 9.00, Courtroom II.
